questions.topic: Diagnosing a reversed-bound subtraction
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose reversed bounds
questions.stem: In an audit report, explain why swapping bounds in a definite integral flips the sign.

answer.exemplar: By definition integral from a to b is F(b)-F(a), and integral from b to a is F(a)-F(b), which is the negative. Thus swapping bounds multiplies the value by -1. This is a common sign error in reports.

questions.explanation: The definition gives F(b)-F(a); reversing gives F(a)-F(b) = -(F(b)-F(a)). The sign flips.
